test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

That movie is so sad; the ending always __makes me bawling__.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3' **i.e.** 'makes me bawl'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct improvement for the underlined part of the sentence is option 3) **"makes me bawl."**
 
• **The original sentence,** "That movie is so sad; the ending always **makes me bawling," **is** incorrect because** the phrase **"makes me bawling"** improperly uses the progressive form of the verb "bawl" (which means to cry loudly) after "makes me."
 
• In English, the **base form of the verb** (also known as the infinitive without "to") should follow **"makes me."**

Therefore, the** correct sentence **is: "*That movie is so sad; the ending always makes me bawl."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1) "makes me bawled"** is incorrect because "bawled" is the past tense form of "bawl," which does not fit in this context.
 
• **Option 4) "made me bawl" **changes the tense of the sentence from present to past, altering the original meaning. The original sentence indicates that the movie consistently (always) has this effect, which is a present tense context.
